# Blaise 1.10.0: timecode links, backups, a Claude connector, and notes language
Four features in one release. Your meetings, transcripts, notes and settings carry over untouched; the library gets one new table for the timecode links on first launch.
## What changed
- **Timecode links.** Hover an item in the notes (a paragraph, a decision or an action item) and a small play mark appears beside it. Click it and the recording plays from 3 seconds before that moment; click again to pause. The notes don't scroll and nothing gets selected. Right-click a paragraph for "Play from m:ss", and VoiceOver reads each mark as a button. New notes get their marks automatically, through one extra call on the Claude subscription engine. "Generate Timestamps" adds them to a meeting from before this version. Turn it off with "Link notes to the recording" in Settings. - **Backups.** A new Backup tab. Pick a folder, and Blaise backs up your library there every day. Encryption is optional: Blaise generates the password, shows it once (copy or print it), and keeps it in your login Keychain. Restore any backup from the same tab; your current library is set aside, not deleted. - **Connect to Claude.** "Connect to Claude…" sets up a read-only connector so Claude Desktop and Claude Code can search your meetings and read their notes, action items and transcripts. It never changes anything in Blaise. - **Notes language.** Choose Auto, English or Portuguese for your notes. It applies to new notes and to notes you regenerate yourself; existing notes are never rewritten in bulk. - **Upgrading from 1.9.2:** delivered in place by the updater.
## Assets
- `Blaise-1.10.0.zip`: the notarised, stapled app (macOS 15.6.1+, Apple Silicon) - `blaise-meet-extension.zip`: the Chrome extension for Google Meet participant/speaker signals (unchanged)

# Blaise 1.9.2: a faster notes pane, and corrections across paragraphs
The notes pane is rebuilt as a single text view. Long notes open and scroll much faster, and AI Correct and Add Note now work on a selection that spans several paragraphs.
## What changed
- **Faster notes.** On a large test note (about 20,000 characters), opening goes from about 2 s to 0.65 s, a click answers in about 5 ms instead of 200 ms, and scrolling runs at 120 fps without stutter. Very long notes that used to hang now open in a fraction of a second. - **AI Correct and Add Note across paragraphs.** Drag across bullets, paragraphs or sections and correct or annotate the whole passage. The composer opens under the last paragraph you selected, and every selected piece is highlighted. - **Selection and pointer behave like any Mac text app.** The selection follows your drag, the text cursor shows over words and the normal pointer everywhere else. - **Checklist clicks tick, they don't aim.** Clicking an item in your action items no longer brings up the AI bar; select words or right-click to correct one. - **All four looks** (Aquarela, Estúdio, Caderno, Fluido) keep their typography, section chrome and motion. - **Fixed:** the end of a paragraph could be hidden under a note card or pending correction. - **Upgrading from 1.9.1:** delivered in place by the updater. Meetings, transcripts, notes and settings untouched.
## Assets
- `Blaise-1.9.2.zip`: the notarised, stapled app (macOS 15.6.1+, Apple Silicon) - `blaise-meet-extension.zip`: the Chrome extension for Google Meet participant/speaker signals (unchanged)

# Blaise 1.9.1: notes on Sonnet 5.5
The Claude subscription engine now writes your notes and memory digest with Sonnet 5.5.
## What changed
- **Sonnet 5.5 for the subscription engine.** In side-by-side tests on real meetings, 5.5 wrote more accurate notes and digests than 4.6 (fewer wrong names, dates and superseded decisions kept as if still decided) and finished in about half the time. The API engine stays on Sonnet 4.6. - **Room for long meetings.** The engine's output limit goes up to 32,000 tokens, so the digest of a two-hour meeting is no longer cut short. - **Your own commitments land in your action items.** A new notes prompt version, c6-v1.2, treats anything you say you will do yourself ("I'll…", "vou…") as your action item, even when you say it in passing. It is the new default for every engine; the earlier versions stay selectable. - **Upgrading from 1.9.0:** delivered in place by the updater. Meetings, transcripts, notes and settings untouched.
## Assets
- `Blaise-1.9.1.zip`: the notarised, stapled app (macOS 15.6.1+, Apple Silicon) - `blaise-meet-extension.zip`: the Chrome extension for Google Meet participant/speaker signals (unchanged)
